subject: Banking
title: Subprime: Lending to Lose
description: A 60-second lesson on Subprime: Lending to Lose.

hook.text: Banks gave mortgages to people who couldn't repay them, then sold those mortgages as 'safe' investments.

buildup.text: Subprime lenders offered 'teaser' rates: 1-2% for two years, then jumping to 8-10%.

discovery.text: Countrywide Financial originated $97 billion in subprime loans in one year. Volume meant commissions.

twist.text: Loan officers earned commissions for every loan closed, regardless of repayment.

climax.text: Subprime lending wasn't just risky. It was designed to extract fees from people who couldn't afford the terms.

punchline.text: $97 billion in bad loans. Designed to collect fees, not to be repaid.

quiz.question: Why did banks issue subprime mortgages to people who couldn't repay?
options: Loan officers earned commissions per loan regardless of repayment
